How much does planning software cost?

Compare prices for financial advisers (people who help clients plan their money). We show a one-person price only when the vendor says what that price covers.

PRICE CHECKED 16 OCTOBER 202620 PRODUCTSNO PAID SOURCES USED
Quick answer

14 products have at least one current numeric price or fee. The other six are quote-only, unpublished, limited to a Voya-branded page with billing terms unstated, or historical. Billing units differ, so a smaller dollar amount is not automatically a better deal.

First, check what you get for the price.

Some companies charge for each adviser or login. Others charge one price for a whole firm, for each task, or for managing client money. A cheaper plan may do less. We keep unlike prices separate.

The 14 current numeric offers/fees use different meters: per adviser, firm, usage, consumer subscription, or managed assets. They are not 14 directly comparable software plans. The six at the end have no standard public price (including eMoney’s Voya-page offer with unstated eligibility/unit) or only an InStream historical price.
KEY TERMS

Use the same language in the meeting.

Open this short guide when a price label or product name is unfamiliar.

Open the plain-language guide
Voya-channel

This report’s shorthand for the eMoney offer shown on its Voya-branded page. That page lists prices, but does not say who qualifies, what one monthly price covers, or the contract term. It is not a standard eMoney rate card.

EMX and EMX Pro

These are names of two eMoney offers; the page does not explain what “EMX” stands for. It lists EMX at $200/month for comparing goal options and EMX Pro at $266/month for presenting estate-planning techniques and advanced planning. Both list a dashboard, digital advice, mobile app, reports, client portal, lead capture, document storage, screen sharing, account aggregation and integrations. The page does not state eligibility, billing unit, or contract term. See the Voya-branded offer page.

Seat / per adviser / per user

One paid login for one person. It is not automatically the whole firm’s bill.

Firm price

A price for the practice or organization. Do not divide it by the number of advisers unless the company says how many are included.

Credit / Snapshot

A prepaid unit for a specific piece of work. Different companies can define each unit differently; it is not a user login.

Add-on

An extra feature or service bought in addition to the main plan; check whether the base package already includes it.

Annualized price

A monthly amount multiplied by 12 to estimate a year. It is our calculation, not necessarily a yearly price the company offers.

Quote-only / not publicly listed

The company asks buyers to contact sales or sign a contract before seeing a price. “Not listed” does not mean free.

AUM fee

A fee based on assets under management—the client money an adviser manages. It is an advice fee, not the price of planning software.

Survey reach, not market share

For T3, the report’s individual “market share” figure is the share of 2,906 valid respondents who provided a rating for that product. It is not the share of firms using it or paid seats; respondents may rate more than one tool.

Consumer plan / advice

A plan sold to a person or household, or a fee for a human advice service. It is not the same product as adviser-office software.

Historical price

A past price for a product that has closed or changed. It helps explain the record; it is not a price a new buyer can get today.

Survey measures for all 20 products

T3 / Inside Information 2026: The report’s individual “market share” metric counts advisors who provided a product rating divided by all 2,906 valid respondents—not firms within that product category or verified current paid customers. Fieldwork ran November–December 2025 and January through the first half of February 2026; respondent geography is not stated. The report lists FP Alpha, SEI, Orion, Advyzon, Practifi and Jump as 2026 sponsors. Its category-penetration figures separately count respondents using at least one solution: Financial Planning Software 83.30%, AI Notetaking 42.86%, and Client Communication Power Tools 2.72%. What can change the price

A seat is one paid login for one person. A credit is a prepaid unit that pays for a set amount of work; each company can define that work differently. AI (artificial intelligence) means software that can sort information or draft text. Account linking brings accounts from banks and other financial companies into one place. A company package may cover several people, but the number included may be unknown.

Other kinds of prices

A whole-company price is not a price for one person. A credit pack pays for a set amount of work; it does not buy unlimited accounts. Advice fees based on client money are not software prices.

Firm packageFP Alpha All-in-One: $1,995/year for a firm license with 55 credits and unlimited logins.
Flat monthly planElements Core: $149/month, or an estimated $1,788 for 12 months. The company has not said how many people are included.
Usage / creditsFP Alpha charges for packs of work units called credits. The price depends on the kind of document or household review.
Managed adviceEmpower charges a small share of the client money it manages. The amount depends on how much money there is and which plan applies.

For some plans, we multiplied the published monthly package price by 12. That gives an estimated 12-month bill for the whole plan, not the price for one person. Credit packs are work units, not yearly user accounts.

FP Alpha: how work credits affect the bill

One All-in-One plan includes 55 credits and unlimited user accounts. The whole firm shares the credits. A credit is a prepaid work unit, but one credit may cover a different kind of work in each pack.

PackCreditsPublished totalAverage cost for one credit
We divided each pack price by the number of credits inside it. This is the average cost of a credit, not the price of buying one extra credit. The company lists extra packs of 10 but does not show their price.[23]

Empower: advice fee based on client money, not software price

Private Client charges different rates on different amounts of money. Enter an amount to see an estimated yearly fee. You may need to invest at least the stated minimum to qualify.

ESTIMATED YEARLY ADVICE FEE
—

Estimated yearly fee on the amount entered. Different parts of the money have different rates: 0.79% on the first $3 million, 0.69% on the next $2 million, 0.59% on the next $5 million, and 0.49% on anything above $10 million. The reported minimum is $1 million. ETF (exchange-traded fund) costs are separate and vary. An ETF is a basket of investments bought together.[31][32]
